title: The questions that had nowhere to land
why: Reported from a live hosted session: asking what books had been ordered got a fluent, confident answer about one order, because the aggregate question had no intent to land in and a hosted model mapped it onto order_status. The safe failure mode never fired — from the state machine's view nothing had gone wrong. Both questions now have a door of their own. Asking the agent its name needed one too: routing it through retrieval would have meant keyword-matching on 'you' and 'your', which makes 'how long do you keep your records?' retrieve the identity article.

turns.reply: Happy to help. I can check an order's status, start a return or refund, or answer questions about shipping, returns, and your account. What would you like to do?
My name is Hal. I can check an order's status, start a return or refund, and answer questions about shipping, returns and your account — anything I can't settle goes to a human colleague.

turns.customer: That sounds great to me. Hey, what books have I ordered in the past?
turns.reply: You've placed 38 orders with us. The most recent are: Dune (BK-1041), Exhalation (BK-2131), Godel, Escher, Bach (BK-1042). There are 35 more — ask me about any of them by title.

turns.customer: Yeah, but what is the total number of books that I have ordered?
turns.reply: You've placed 38 orders with us. The most recent are: Dune (BK-1041), Exhalation (BK-2131), Godel, Escher, Bach (BK-1042). There are 35 more — ask me about any of them by title.

accepted.why: The last two turns ask the same thing two ways — what have I ordered, and how many — and there is one true answer to both. The reply leads with the count, which is what the second question wants. Varying the wording to avoid repeating myself would be decoration, not information.
